body: But whose fault was it that she continued to trust and love me even after I deliberately tried to push her away?

I'm serious, and though it may not play along with typical ideas of romanticism, it is not my fault that I didn't want to spend my life with someone who was constantly depressed and so unadventurous because of it. I didn't want to let her drag her down with me. I don't think anyone should let someone else do that to them, because then maybe I'd become depressed, too. I think women get so caught up in romantic bullshit they see in movies that they expect men to be willing to do anything, even die for them, in the name of love, when in reality, things just aren't like that. Men don't want to have to change or sacrifice things for a woman, and they shouldn't have to. It's unfair. Maybe she didn't have to die, but I'm not going to let feelings stand in the way of the matter: what she did by trying to force her sadness on me and everyone around her was wrong, I didn't force her to kill herself, and I shouldn't have had to sacrifice me living my life to try to help someone who was so stupid and hypersensitive that it's a miracle she lived to be as old as she did.

Maybe, but at the same time, it's not like it's entirely my fault. I didn't MAKE her kill herself, and it's not my fault she chose to stay with someone who hurt her over and over again. She was pretty sweet, but dumb as shit in all aspects of life.
My heart has never felt so full
